assignments.reason: The act of beginning to seek 'where is His glory' is, by essential nature, the act of teshuvah itself. The Rebbe explicitly states (line 18): 'זֶה עִקָּר הַתְּשׁוּבָה, כְּשֶׁאָדָם מְבַקֵּשׁ וּמְחַפֵּשׂ אַחַר כְּבוֹדוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ'. The seeking IS the return — not a separate action that causes return, but the very essence of teshuvah. This node describes the initiation of that seeking process, placing it squarely in the domain of return and ascent.

Reviving oneself from the holy life-force is the essential nature of teshuvah — reconnecting to kedusha from within the fallen state. The Rebbe states (line 21-23) that by seeking 'ayeh' one revives oneself with holy vitality in the very place of one's fall, and this is a bechina of the maamar satum's life-force received through holiness rather than through concealment. The essential nature of this concept is the restoration of holy vitality, which is the substance of teshuvah and the Tree of Life.

Seeking and searching 'where is His glory' is explicitly identified as the essence of teshuvah (line 18): 'וְזֶה בְּחִינוֹת תְּשׁוּבָה, כִּי זֶה עִקָּר הַתְּשׁוּבָה, כְּשֶׁאָדָם מְבַקֵּשׁ וּמְחַפֵּשׂ אַחַר כְּבוֹדוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ'. The essential nature of this node is the active process of return — the searching, longing, and yearning for God's glory that constitutes teshuvah. It belongs to the return/ascent domain.

assignments.node_id: הוא חוזר ועולה אל הכבוד העליון
assignments.reason: Returning and ascending to the supreme glory describes the completion of the teshuvah process. Though the destination is the kavod elyon (Package 1), the essential nature of this node is the act of return and ascent — 'חוזר ועולה' — which is synonymous with teshuvah and with 'יְרִידָה תַּכְלִית הָעֲלִיָּה'. The Rebbe states (line 12): 'בָּזֶה בְּעַצְמוֹ הוּא חוֹזֵר וְעוֹלֶה אֶל הַכָּבוֹד הָעֶלְיוֹן' — the returning-and-ascending IS the teshuvah itself.

assignments.node_id: רק לילך בתמימות ובפשיטות, בלי שום חכמות, ולהסתכל בכל דבר שעושה, שיהיה שם השם יתברך, ולבלי להשגיח כלל על כבוד עצמו. רק אם יש בזה כבוד השם יתברך יעשה, ואם לאו – לאו
assignments.reason: This node is the practical expression of temimut u'peshitut — walking in simplicity, without reliance on one's own wisdom, acting only for God's kavod. The essential nature is identical to the existing package node 'תְּמִימוּת וּפְשִׁיטוּת': it is the correct human orientation toward divine kavod, the fundamental alignment that the Rebbe calls 'עִקָּר הַיַּהֲדוּת' (the essence of Judaism). The criterion 'if there is God's kavod in it, do it; if not, do not' is the direct expression of living for revealed divine glory.

The guarantee of never stumbling is the essential state of one who is aligned with divine kavod through temimut. By essential nature, this describes the protected, stable condition of one who acts only for kevod Hashem — it is the fruit of the temimut-kavod alignment. The Rebbe places this statement (line 2) as the direct consequence of the temimut prescription: 'וַאֲזַי בְּוַדַּאי לֹא יִכָּשֵׁל לְעוֹלָם'. Its essential nature is security within the domain of revealed divine glory.
